text.arabic_uthmani: وَتَرَىٰ كَثِيرًۭا مِّنْهُمْ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ وَأَكْلِهِمُ ٱلسُّحْتَ ۚ لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ

words.gloss_range: coordinating continuation into an observed accusation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps 5:62 joined to the exposure in 5:61 instead of opening a detached topic. It releases directly into the seeing clause, so the conduct that follows is presented as visible continuation of the prior scene.

topics.headline: opening continuation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not begin as a detached accusation; it carries the exposed group from 5:61 into the observed conduct of 5:62.
topics.reason: The opening coordinator and boundary rows tie the new observation to the prior verse rather than to an unrelated topic.

topics.headline: direct witness launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the connector releases immediately into a seeing clause, making the list that follows visible to the addressee.
topics.reason: The particle begins a coordinated observation beat before the direct-address verb.

words.gloss_range: active seeing, perceiving, or witnessing of the group and its conduct
words.root_gloss_range: seeing/perceiving/judging range; local form selects active second-person witnessing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: seen object quantified as many from the group

words.prose: {{ar:تَرَىٰ}} ({{tr:tarā}}) makes the addressee an active, ongoing witness: the verb carries the second-person subject, takes {{ar:كَثِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:kathīran}}) as object, and holds the following racing clause as the seen state. Its perception range lets sight become recognition, and the boundary with 5:61 turns concealed inner posture into visible conduct. Same-surah seeing formulas expose other failures too: the seeing-and-rushing relation is pressured by 5:52, and the same opening frame returns with a different offense in 5:80. The passive-leaning variant is useful only as contrast; the local base wording keeps active witnessing in front.

topics.headline: active ongoing witness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressee is made an active witness of ongoing conduct, not merely told about a closed past event.
topics.reason: The active second-person imperfect has an explicit object and a following circumstantial action, so the conduct is framed as present observation.

topics.headline: sight becoming appraisal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that seeing here includes recognition: the observed motion is prepared for the verdict at the end.
topics.reason: The root range includes seeing and perceiving, and the ayah moves from observation to explicit dispraise.

topics.headline: same-surah seeing formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a Surah 5 exposure pattern: the same seeing formula returns with different failures, including 5:80.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect this opening with same-surah seeing formulas while keeping the local object and action distinct.

topics.headline: concealment answered by sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary movement from what was concealed in 5:61 to conduct made visible in 5:62.
topics.reason: The boundary rows repeatedly contrast prior concealment with the present seeing clause.

topics.headline: active base with passive variant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a passive reading marks the scene as shown, while the base wording keeps the addressee actively seeing.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as contrast, but the local base parse remains active.

words.gloss_range: many as a substantial but scoped subset, functioning as the seen object
words.root_gloss_range: abundance and multiplicity; local phrase blocks totality

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: partitive phrase narrowing the many to a subset

words.prose: {{ar:كَثِيرًۭا}} ({{tr:kathīran}}) is the seen object, a large quantity that is immediately scoped by {{ar:مِّنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}). The word therefore creates social scale without saying all of them, leaving room for the measured-minority contrast noted at 5:66. Its singular quantity then expands through the plural racing verb, so the reader sees one mass and many actors at once; the same Surah 5 many-among-them formula also appears in diagnostic settings such as 5:64 and 5:80.

topics.headline: many as seen subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accusation is large-scale but not totalizing: many are seen, yet the following partitive keeps the charge scoped.
topics.reason: The accusative object is immediately narrowed by the partitive phrase, preserving both scale and limit.

topics.headline: singular quantity acting plurally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a singular quantity turning into plural actors when the racing verb arrives.
topics.reason: The local syntax allows the quantity to be the object of seeing while the following plural verb distributes action across the group.

topics.headline: abundance as social scale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wrong is not a private lapse but a widespread social pattern within the referenced group.
topics.reason: The root and distributional rows support abundance and group-scale judgment without making the scope total.

topics.headline: many among them refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recurring Surah 5 diagnostic frame in which many among a group are marked by different failures, including 5:64 and 5:80.
topics.reason: The same-surah rows preserve the repeated formula while the local clause specifies racing into wrongdoing.

words.gloss_range: partitive from them; subset selection with pronoun continuity
words.prose: {{ar:مِّنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) does two jobs at once: it carries the prior group forward through the suffix and limits the accusation through the partitive preposition. The syntax narrows the group before the racing is described, so the verse preserves continuity with 5:61 without totalizing the charge.

topics.headline: partitive pronoun bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pronoun carries the prior group into the verse while the preposition limits the charge to a subset.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the pronoun as a partitive complement of the quantity and also carries the antecedent from the prior discourse.

topics.headline: scope fixed before action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first fixes who is being discussed before naming what they do.
topics.reason: The fused preposition-suffix unit follows the quantity and precedes the racing clause.

words.gloss_range: racing or vying in haste, locally routed within sin
words.root_gloss_range: speed/eagerness/rivalry range; local Form III and prepositional complement make culpable competition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition routing the racing into its moral domain

words.prose: {{ar:يُسَٰرِعُونَ}} ({{tr:yusāriʿūna}}) shows the many in motion while they are being seen. Because it is completed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) rather than a simple goal marker, the racing takes place inside the field that follows. Form III adds a competitive or reciprocal pressure: they are not merely quick but vying in culpable movement. Surah 5 uses this rushing motif in 5:41, 5:52, and 5:62, while positive racing scenes such as 3:114 and 21:90 show that urgency itself is redirected here toward the wrong field. The long medial beat of the form also lets the rushing occupy audible space before landing in the condemned domain, carrying the prior hidden posture into public momentum.

topics.headline: racing inside the field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not merely aim toward sin from outside; the racing is placed within the moral field named after it.
topics.reason: The verb is locally completed by the preposition, and the complement supplies the culpable field that changes speed into moral eagerness.

topics.headline: moving scene of many
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the many are visible as an acting collective while the addressee sees them in the act.
topics.reason: The imperfect plural is a circumstantial clause describing the seen quantity.

topics.headline: competitive haste
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form depicts vying or competing in the wrong, not just moving quickly.
topics.reason: The base Form III supports reciprocal racing, while the variant exposes the simpler acceleration contrast.

topics.headline: Surah 5 rushing motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rushing is a repeated Surah 5 diagnostic motif, with 5:41, 5:52, and 5:62 naming different fields of culpable movement.
topics.reason: The contextual rows identify a same-surah series while the local complement narrows this occurrence to sin.

topics.headline: urgency reversed by target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same urgency can be praised elsewhere but here is inverted because its target is sin, unlike racing to good in 3:114 and 21:90.
topics.reason: The occurrence rows preserve the good-versus-bad direction contrast without changing the local negative field.

topics.headline: audible and boundary momentum
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the long racing form carries prior concealed posture into open public momentum.
topics.reason: The phonetic and boundary rows support a secondary observation about pacing and outward manifestation.

words.gloss_range: in or into as the domain marker for the racing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first governed accusation and domain of the racing

words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) is the hinge that turns speed into moral location. It governs {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithm}}) and keeps the motion inside, or deeper into, the domain of sin rather than merely pointed toward it from outside. Its short form also binds the verb tightly to the first accusation.

topics.headline: in rather than merely toward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition makes the wrong an enclosing domain, with motion inside or deeper into it rather than a distant endpoint.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the first abstract noun and attaches to the rushing verb, routing motion into the moral domain.

topics.headline: compressed governed link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how tightly the short preposition binds the racing verb to the first accusation.
topics.reason: The form and recitation rows support a compact attachment between motion and governed noun.

words.gloss_range: sin or culpable wrongdoing as a definite governed domain
words.root_gloss_range: guilt/sin with a slowing-from-good image; local gerund selects moral category
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithm}}) names a definite field of sin under the preposition, not an isolated label for the actors. The root image of guilt as heaviness or slowing from good sharpens the irony: they hurry into what burdens and retards. As the first item in {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithm}}) and {{ar:ٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿudwān}}), it opens a known pair also seen in 5:2, 2:85, and 58:8-9, then begins the list’s movement from moral category toward material practice.

topics.headline: known moral field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sin is named as a definite recognizable field, not as an indefinite misstep.
topics.reason: The definite gerund is governed by the preposition and functions as a category of conduct.

topics.headline: racing into what slows
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that they hurry into a word field associated with guilt and being slowed from good, while the local sense remains sin.
topics.reason: The root-image rows color the local sin sense; they do not replace it with physical slowness.

topics.headline: sin and aggression pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first two accusations as a recognizable pair joining inward culpability with outward boundary violation, also seen in 5:2, 2:85, and 58:8-9.
topics.reason: The conjoined genitives and recurrence rows support the paired moral formula.

topics.headline: start of escalation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list starting from abstract moral violation before moving outward and then material.
topics.reason: The first item begins the tripartite sequence that later becomes concrete consuming.

words.gloss_range: coordination linking the first two abstract accusations

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first abstract accusation joined by the connector
second abstract accusation joined to the first

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins {{ar:ٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿudwān}}) to {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithm}}) under the same governed frame. It makes the first two accusations a coupled unit before the second connector adds the concrete consuming phrase.

topics.headline: first internal connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first internal connector turns sin and aggression into a coupled indictment under the same scope.
topics.reason: The coordinator links the second abstract noun to the first under the prepositional frame.

topics.headline: repeated list hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated connectors creating a two-hinge frame for the three accusations.
topics.reason: The two internal coordinators structure the movement from the paired abstractions to the concrete third item.

words.gloss_range: transgression, aggression, and boundary violation as the second governed field
words.root_gloss_range: crossing/enmity/aggression range; local gerund selects moral overreach

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: paired first accusation under the same prepositional scope

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعُدْوَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-ʿudwān}}) is a definite gerund parallel to {{ar:ٱلْإِثْمِ}} ({{tr:al-ithm}}), still inside the same prepositional scope. Its root field of crossing, hostility, and overreach makes the second charge outward and relational, while local grammar keeps it an abstract category of transgression. A vowel variant tests the recitational shape without changing that category. The pair prohibited in 5:2 is now observed as conduct in 5:62, and this middle term carries the list from inner guilt toward material consumption.

topics.headline: recognized aggression category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that transgression is a definite, governed category paired with sin rather than an independent new clause.
topics.reason: The definite gerund remains genitive as the coordinated partner of the first accusation.

topics.headline: crossing with hostility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root field of crossing, aggression, and enmity behind the local sense of transgression; the local grammar keeps it as an abstract moral category.
topics.reason: The broader root field enriches the local category without turning it into literal running, enmity alone, or contagion.

topics.headline: forbidden pair now observed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pair prohibited in 5:2 appears here as observed conduct, with wider formula parallels at 2:85 and 58:8.
topics.reason: The echo rows identify the same pair in prohibition and violation settings.

topics.headline: middle of escalation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the middle term mediating between inner guilt and material illicit consumption.
topics.reason: Its position connects backward to the paired abstraction and forward to the concrete phrase.

topics.headline: stable category with vowel variant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a vowel variant marks recitational pressure while leaving the transgression category intact.
topics.reason: The variant changes vocalization, not the local root or category.

words.gloss_range: coordination adding the concrete third accusation
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the third accusation rather than replacing the first two. The connector marks the turn from paired abstract fields to a heavier possessive verbal-noun phrase, so the list lands in a concrete economic practice.

topics.headline: third list turn
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list turning from paired abstract wrongs to an embodied practice of illicit consumption.
topics.reason: The second internal coordinator adds a possessive verbal-noun phrase as the third item.

topics.headline: audible tripartite frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two connectors as rails that let the indictment accumulate in three distinct steps.
topics.reason: The repeated particle frames the sequence without collapsing the items.

words.gloss_range: their consuming as a verbal noun with agent suffix and object
words.root_gloss_range: eating/consuming/eating-away range; local object narrows it to illicit economic devouring

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite object consumed by the verbal noun

words.prose: {{ar:أَكْلِهِمُ}} ({{tr:aklihim}}) names their own consuming: the verbal noun carries the group as agent through its suffix and governs {{ar:ٱلسُّحْتَ}} ({{tr:al-suḥt}}) as object. Eating vocabulary becomes economic devouring here, not ordinary nourishment. The phrase recurs in the Surah 5 cluster around 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, where corrupt listening, consuming, and failure to restrain are held around the same illicit practice.

topics.headline: possessed act with object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase names their own consuming as an act directed toward a specific object, not a vague corruption.
topics.reason: The verbal noun has an agentive suffix and governs the following definite object.

topics.headline: eating as exploitation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices ordinary eating vocabulary becoming an image of economic devouring and destructive transfer.
topics.reason: The root rows support consuming and eating-away imagery, locally narrowed by the illicit object.

topics.headline: Surah 5 illicit-consumption cluster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase recurring around 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, moving between listeners, consumers, and those who should restrain them.
topics.reason: The collocation rows show a tight same-surah cluster for eating destructive gain.

topics.headline: concrete climax of the list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the third item giving the indictment actors, act, and object after two abstractions.
topics.reason: The phrase is the list’s concrete peak before the verdict.

words.gloss_range: the definite illicit/destructive gain consumed by them
words.root_gloss_range: scraping, uprooting, destroying; local noun names destructive forbidden gain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: possessive verbal noun governing the illicit object

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسُّحْتَ}} ({{tr:al-suḥt}}) fixes the object of {{ar:أَكْلِهِمُ}} ({{tr:aklihim}}) as a definite class of destructive forbidden gain. The root imagery of scraping bare, uprooting, and destroying makes the consumed gain itself corrosive. Its rarity matters: the noun is concentrated in 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, with a destruction-root echo at 20:61, so the final concrete charge is locally load-bearing before the verdict generalizes it. Variant vocalizations change the word's recitational weight without changing the destructive-gain sense, and the term externalizes the concealed failure of 5:61 as a material economy of erasure.

topics.headline: named illicit object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the consuming phrase closing on a definite named object, not on generic appetite or unspecified wealth.
topics.reason: The accusative object is definite and becomes the final concrete charge before the verdict.

topics.headline: destructive gain image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices illicit gain imagined as something that scrapes bare, uproots, and destroys blessing while being consumed.
topics.reason: The root-image rows and the preceding eating noun converge on destructive acquisition.

topics.headline: rare Surah 5 term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the noun is rare and concentrated in the Surah 5 cluster at 5:42, 5:62, and 5:63, with a verbal destruction echo at 20:61.
topics.reason: The low-occurrence profile and critical rows make the term locally load-bearing and tied to adjacent verses.

topics.headline: stable sense across vocalizations
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices variant vocalizations as sound-form pressure while the destructive-gain sense remains stable.
topics.reason: The variants change vocalic weight and sound texture but do not change the local object role.

topics.headline: concealment becomes material erasure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices hidden failure from 5:61 externalized as a material economy of destructive gain in 5:62.
topics.reason: The boundary row links prior covering imagery with the local destructive-gain term.

words.gloss_range: emphatic lām prefixed to the dispraise verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) fuses emphasis to the dispraise verb and starts the ayah’s turn from list to judgment. The close is therefore introduced as an emphatically asserted verdict on the conduct just enumerated.

topics.headline: emphasis before dispraise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict is emphatically asserted before the dispraise verb even arrives.
topics.reason: The bound emphatic particle scopes over the formal dispraise construction.

topics.headline: hinge from list to verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural turn from enumerating conduct to judging the whole pattern.
topics.reason: The particle opens the final judgment unit after the last concrete charge.

words.gloss_range: fixed verb of dispraise in an emphatic condemnation formula
words.root_gloss_range: badness, wretchedness, severity; local uninflected form selects formal dispraise

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following subject or content of the dispraise formula

words.prose: {{ar:بِئْسَ}} ({{tr:biʾsa}}) is the formal verb of dispraise, strengthened by the preceding emphatic particle and completed by the following {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) clause. Its severity root colors the verdict as wretched and weighty, while the fixed construction keeps the local function as condemnation. The same formula clusters in Surah 5, including 5:63, 5:79, and 5:80, and here it gathers the tripartite list into an evaluative landing. The hamza catch is a sound pressure point: the smoothed variant eases the pronunciation without changing the verdict.

topics.headline: formal dispraise construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the close is not a neutral summary; it is a formal grammar of condemnation requiring the following content.
topics.reason: The uninflected dispraise verb combines with emphasis and receives its subject/content from the following clause.

topics.headline: wretchedness with severity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root field of badness, misery, and severity behind the local dispraise formula, while the fixed construction selects condemnation.
topics.reason: The root range enriches the verdict but the local form is the fixed verb of dispraise.

topics.headline: Surah 5 verdict refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same emphatic dispraise formula recurring in Surah 5 closures, including 5:63, 5:79, and 5:80.
topics.reason: The occurrence rows show a same-surah cluster and wider formulaic dispraise use.

topics.headline: specifics gathered into verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final formula gathering the detailed accusations into a concise judgment on what they were doing.
topics.reason: The tadhyil-like tail converts the tripartite list into a habitual-conduct verdict.

topics.headline: hamza as sound pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the glottal catch as a recitational pressure point, while the variant smooths sound without changing the verdict.
topics.reason: The base and variant forms differ phonetically, not semantically in the local formula.

words.gloss_range: what/that which gathers the condemned content
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) supplies the content condemned by the dispraise formula: not one item from the list, but the whole pattern of what they were doing. Its relative and maṣdariyya possibilities both work toward that coverage, either pointing to the deeds as content or nominalizing the doing itself. The same frame returns in 5:63 with a different closing verb.

topics.headline: what as condemned content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict’s target is not one item from the list but the whole content gathered as what they were doing.
topics.reason: The pronoun functions as subject or relative content for the dispraise verb and compresses the prior list.

topics.headline: content and doing readings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle can point to the deeds as content or nominalize the doing itself, and both readings keep the verdict focused on conduct.
topics.reason: The two parses differ in route, but both cover the condemned behavior rather than introducing a new object.

topics.headline: adjacent verdict frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same frame returning in 5:63, with the closing verb carrying the local contrast.
topics.reason: The adjacent-verse rows preserve the formulaic repetition and verb variation.

words.gloss_range: past auxiliary framing the final imperfect as habitual practice
words.root_gloss_range: being/existence/state; local auxiliary gives persisted past aspect
words.prose: {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}) frames the final imperfect as habitual past practice. It does not add a separate act; it makes the doing a persisted state belonging to the same plural group carried through the ayah. As part of a familiar condemnation pattern, the auxiliary lets the dispraise judge persisted conduct rather than a momentary act. It also links the boundary from habitual concealment in 5:61 to habitual doing in 5:62, holding the clause open until the final action word arrives.

topics.headline: habitual past frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict condemns an established practice over time, not one isolated incident.
topics.reason: The perfect auxiliary governs the imperfect predicate and frames the final action as persisted past practice.

topics.headline: plural group carried through
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same plural actors seen at the start remain the owners of the habitual verdict.
topics.reason: The plural marker keeps the auxiliary attached to the group chain.

topics.headline: habitual verdict formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a familiar condemnation pattern in which being plus doing lets the dispraise judge more than a moment.
topics.reason: The contextual rows show repeated pairings with deed and dispraise vocabulary.

topics.headline: habitual concealment to habitual doing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary echo from 5:61’s habitual concealment to 5:62’s habitual doing.
topics.reason: The boundary rows link the same auxiliary pattern across the verse boundary.

topics.headline: delay before final action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the auxiliary holding the closing clause open until the final action word lands.
topics.reason: The word order gives the final predicate closure weight.

words.gloss_range: doing, working, or purposeful action as the final summary of conduct
words.root_gloss_range: action/work/production; local imperfect after auxiliary selects habitual purposeful doing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: auxiliary that frames the final imperfect as habitual past

words.prose: {{ar:يَعْمَلُونَ}} ({{tr:yaʿmalūna}}) closes the ayah by gathering sin, transgression, and consuming destructive gain into broad purposeful doing. After {{ar:كَانُوا۟}} ({{tr:kānū}}), the imperfect marks habitual practice, not a one-time event; the plural ending keeps the same many in view. The verb choice matters beside 5:63 and 5:79: 5:62 closes with broad deliberate doing, while the neighboring formulas vary the final action term. The ayah thus moves from witnessed conduct at the opening to judged accountable action at the close.

topics.headline: habitual doing as verdict content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb summarizes the listed acts as sustained practice rather than a single completed deed.
topics.reason: The imperfect predicate after the auxiliary receives the content from the preceding particle and belongs to a habitual judgment formula.

topics.headline: same group at closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final plural verb returning to the same many first seen racing.
topics.reason: The plural ending carries the subject chain through the final word.

topics.headline: deliberate practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing word frames the condemned behavior as purposeful doing or work, not accidental occurrence.
topics.reason: The root and form rows support deliberate action broad enough to gather the prior charges.

topics.headline: doing versus making and acting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:62 uses broad purposeful doing, while 5:63 uses crafting/making and 5:79 uses general acting.
topics.reason: The near-synonym rows preserve a same-surah contrast in closing verbs.

topics.headline: specifics recapped as doing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closing by moving from specific accusations back to a general category of accountable conduct.
topics.reason: The final position and broad verb recapitulate the tripartite list.

topics.headline: witness and doing bookend
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from witnessed conduct at the opening to judged doing at the close.
topics.reason: The boundary and echo rows connect opening perception with closing action.

baseline_models.mechanism: Collective haste is yoked to a root image of lagging behind good and then given a boundary-crossing vector: the motion is fast, but its moral result is accelerated backwardness.

activation_trace.role: Speed as the opposite of slowness supplies the overt velocity of the plural action.
Delay from good supplies the paradoxical destination: their haste makes them fall behind good faster.
Crossing a limit in injustice turns raw speed into directed transgression.

changed_reading.before: They quickly commit sin and aggression.
changed_reading.after: Their coordinated haste is itself a mechanism that rapidly carries them into moral lateness and across protective limits.

baseline_models.mechanism: The eating construction can denote taking and consuming wealth, while suht can denote stripping away and eradication. The intake therefore consumes not only an illicit object but the protected basis from which value is drawn.

activation_trace.role: Consumption and taking of wealth supplies the acquisitive intake.
Stripping, removal, and eradication make that intake corrosive to its own source.
Dealings between people locate the corrosive intake within repeatable social transactions.

changed_reading.after: Their illicit intake is extractive: a social transaction that strips away the very protections and sources on which continued exchange depends.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَتَرَىٰ كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُمْ ... مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: Perception frames a numerous cohort whose intentional work is present across time. The ayah diagnoses an observable, repeated practice rather than an invisible essence or a single lapse.

activation_trace.role: Seeing by eye or insight makes conduct, rather than hidden identity, the evidentiary surface.
Growth of number marks a large but bounded cohort within the larger group.

strongest_changes: Speed became a paradoxical engine of delay from good and boundary crossing, not merely intensity.

summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly returned to the focus's observation, many, eating, bad-work, and transgression language while supplying opposed flow systems and opposed visible response cohorts; this made a process reading stronger than a static catalogue of vices.
remaining_uncertainties: The causal arrows from concealment, non-restraint, and sensory closure to acceleration are reader-supplied, even though their sequence is packet-grounded.
The circulation model may be stronger as a moral-economic analogy than as a single lexical synthesis.
The contagion and combustion outliers depend on form-distant branches and must remain explicitly exploratory.

I infer a causal chain: failure to move toward good redirects speed (`س ر ع B001`) across limits and into extractive intake.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Their speed is itself a form of lag.** Fixed **ء ث م / B001** (“slowing and lagging from good”) sits as the destination of *yusāriʿūna*, producing a directional paradox: they hurry into what delays them from good. The ayah then joins overstepping and consumption of illicit gain; 5:63 shows authorities failing to apply a stop. I infer that speed has no positive value apart from its vector. The scene reads as energetic moral retardation, not merely energetic wrongdoing.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:63 supplied the missing endpoint, and 5:64 showed the consequence of its absence expanding into corrupt claims, enmity, war-fire, and movement through the land.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın görme çekirdeği ile doğrudan göz tanıklığını ve görmeye çalışma bildiren bağlı kullanımlar birbirine karıştırılmaz.

root_profile.summary: Kök, suya kanma ve su taşıma çevresinden söz aktarma, düşünerek değerlendirme, ihtiyaç, kalan miktar, yük bağı, yapı bağımlı dolgunluk, görünüş, koku, hayvan, bayrak, uyak harfi, yağmur bulutu ve toplumsal yük taşıyan önderlere uzanan çok sayıda bağımsız dal içerir. Dalların bir bölümü su, taşıma ve doluluk benzetileriyle tarihsel olarak ilişkilendirilebilse de çağdaş kavram haritasında ayrı sınırlar gerektirir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, çokluğu azlığın karşıtı ve sayının artması olarak kurar; ayrıca bir şeyin çok duruma gelmesini, çok duruma getirilmesini ve ondan çokça edinilmesini de açıkça kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın çokluk çekirdeğini öne alır; artırma, çokça edinme ve azıyla çoğunu birlikte anan kalıp ayrı bağımlı kullanımlar olarak korunur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin ya da ayrık bir niceliğin az olmayacak ölçüde bulunması veya sayıca artmasıdır. Buna bir şeyi çok duruma getirme ve ondan çokça edinme gibi bu çekirdekten türeyen işlemler de bağlanır.

facets.statement: Çokluk, azlığın karşıtıdır ve özellikle sayılabilen varlıklarda sayının yüksekliğini ya da artışını bildirir.
Bir şey çok duruma gelebilir, bir başkası onu çok duruma getirebilir veya kişi ondan çokça edinebilir.
Az ve çok, malın ya da içinde bulunulan durumun iki karşıt ölçüsünü birlikte anan kalıpta kullanılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar çokluğu azlığın karşıtı, sayının artması ve bir şeyin çok olması diye ortaklaştırır; ayrıca çoklaştırma, çokça edinme ve çokluk bildiren niteleme biçimlerini aynı anlam alanına bağlar.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه كثرة الشيء والعدد والمال، وضد القلة، والوصف بكثير وكثار وكاثر، وجعل الشيء كثيرا أو الاستكثار منه.
branches.source_phrase_ar: الكثرة نماء العدد (ayn;tahdhib)؛ الكثير ضد القليل (jamhara)؛ الكثرة نقيض القلة (sihah)؛ أصل صحيح يدل خلاف القلة (maqayis)؛ الكثرة والقلة يستعملان في الكمية المنفصلة كالأعداد (mufradat)؛ كثر الشيء كثرة فهو كثير (ayn;sihah;tahdhib)؛ أكثرت الشيء وكثرته جعلته كثيرا (ayn;tahdhib)؛ استكثرت من الشيء أي أكثرت منه (sihah)؛ عدد كثار وكثير وكاثر (jamhara;sihah;mufradat;maqayis)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه كاثرناهم فكثرناهم، ومكاثرة القوم إذا غلبوا غيرهم بالعدد، والتكاثر والتفاخر أو التباري بكثرة العدد والمال والعز.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه مكثر أو كاثر بمعنى كثير المال، ومكثار في كثرة الكلام، ومكثور عليه لكثرة طالبي المعروف أو الحقوق عليه، ويتكثر بمال غيره.
يدخل فيه الكوثر بوصفه نهر الجنة، أو الخير الكثير العظيم، أو الرجل السيد السخي الكثير الخير والعطاء، وكل ذلك من فوعل الكثرة.
يدخل فيه الكوثر من الغبار إذا كثر وثار أو سطع، وتكوثر الشيء إذا كثر كثرة متناهية.
يدخل فيه الكثر أو الكثر بمعنى جمار النخل، والجذب، وطلع النخل عند بعض المصادر، وما ورد في لا قطع في ثمر ولا كثر.
يدخل فيه الكمثرة بمعنى اجتماع الشيء، مع تصريح Maqāyīs بأن الميم زائدة وأنه من الكثرة.

Ayrıca özel ırmak ve bol iyilik, yoğun toz, hurma ağacının iç göbeği ve bir araya toplanma gibi sözlükselleşmiş ayrı dallar bulunur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bu dalın çekirdeğini yavaşlığın karşıtı olan hız olarak açıkça kurar; hareketi, konuşmayı ve başka eylemleri hızlandırmayı, ayrıca su ile yağmurun hızlı akışını kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım genel hız çekirdeğini korur; yönelme, yürüme, yazma, hesap ve ceza gibi kullanımları yalnız kendi yapıları içinde belirtir.

Suyun hızlı akması ve yağmurun hızla boşalması doğal süreçlerdeki örneklerdir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yavaşlığın karşıtı olma konusunda birleşir ve anlamı hem hareket eden varlıklara hem de yapılan işlere taşır. Yürüme, konuşma, yazma, su ve yağmur örnekleri aynı hız çekirdeğini somutlaştırır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه عاد ورجع، والعودة، والعود بعد البدء، والمعاودة، والإعادة، واستعادة الشيء، وتعاود القوم، وعودة الحمى والمسألة، وصيغة عواد وعد، والعوادة من الطعام المعاد.
يدخل فيه المعاد بمعنى المصير والمرجع، والزمان أو المكان الذي يعود إليه، ومعاد الحاج، ومعاد مكة أو الآخرة والجنة في نقل المصادر.
يدخل فيه قولهم ما يبدئ وما يعيد أو لا يبدي ولا يعيد بمعنى لا يتكلم ببادئة ولا عائدة.
يدخل فيه العادة، والاعتياد، والتعود، والدربة حتى تصير سجية، والمواظبة، ومعاودة الحرب، والفحل المعتاد للضراب، والمطيق للشيء لأنه اعتاده.
يدخل فيه عيادة المريض، وعواد المريض، والمعادة في المصيبة أو المأتم التي يغشاها الناس، وما يرجع فيه الزائر مرة بعد مرة.
يدخل فيه العائدة، والمعروف والصلة والفضل، وما عاد على الإنسان بنفع أو رفق أو عطف، وقولهم هذا أعود عليك.
يدخل فيه العيد، والأعياد، وكل يوم مجمع أو يوم سرور، وما يعاود الإنسان من هم أو حب أو حال، وشهود العيد.
يدخل فيه العود من الإبل، والبعير أو الجمل المسن، والناقة أو الشاة أو الفرس في نقل بعض العرب، وما بلغ وقت السن بعد البزول، والاستعارة في الاستعانة بأهل السن والمعرفة.
يدخل فيه الطريق القديم أو العادي، والسؤدد العود، والرحم العود أو العودة بمعنى القديمة، وكل قدم صرحت به المصادر في هذا اللفظ.
يدخل فيه العود من الخشب، وكل خشبة أو خشبة دقيقة في نقل مقاييس، وعود التبخر، والعود الذي يضرب به أو المزهر المعروف.
يدخل فيه العود في الظهار، سواء فسر بتكرار القول، أو الجماع بعد الظهار، أو إمساك المرأة، أو فعل ما حلف ألا يفعله بحسب الأقوال المنقولة.
يدخل فيه عاد القبيلة، والنسبة عادي بمعنى قديم منسوب إلى عاد، واسم عادياء، والإبل العيدية المنسوبة إلى فحل أو إلى عاد بحسب النقل.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişinin dünyadan aldığı payı, geniş geçimliği, kendisine hesap sorulmadan ayrılan şeyi ve yöneticilerin verdiği tahsisatı birlikte gösterir. Dalın pay ve geçimlik çerçevesi bu ortak verilen pay çekirdeğini korur.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiye dünyadan düşen veya kendisine verilen pay, geçimlik ya da tahsisattır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, kişinin elde ettiği pay ve geçimliktir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Kişiye düşen dünya payı, geniş geçimlik veya kendisine ayrılmış tahsisat birlikte kastedildiğinde uygundur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi mal kalıbında harcamayı ve özellikle hakka aykırı sarfı, kişi kalıbında ise başkalarının malını alıp onları sömürmeyi açıkça bir araya getirir. Dal çerçevesi bu iki yapı bağımlı kullanımı doğru korur.

Kişi topluluğuna yönelen yapıda onların malını almak ve onları sömürmek anlatılır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Ateşin odunu yakması, ateşe yakıt verilmesi, alevin şiddetlenmesi ve açıkça belirtilmiş benzetmeli uzantılar birlikte anlatıldığında uygundur.
